title: A Phenomenological Look at Mental Blocks in Artistic Gymnastics
abstract: Mental blocks are a poorly understood but pervasive phenomenon in artistic gymnastics that involve a disconnect between the mind and body and an interference with athletes’ ability to physically perform previously automatic skills. This study used interpretive phenomenological analysis to explore the lived experiences of female, collegiate gymnasts in the United States who have struggled with mental blocks, examining through semistructured interviews how they understand the characteristics and causes of mental blocks and management strategies. Findings suggest that blocks are best understood as a group of phenomena that cannot easily be attributed to a single cause, as they often stem from a combination of factors, such as injuries, fear, pressure, and negative environments. A lack of knowledge and awareness within the sport and mental health resources were noted, as well. Integrating mindset training into coaching could help gymnasts build confidence to navigate mental blocks and prevent mental blocks from occurring.
